turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Doctor Pillay, this is Mrs Naidoo. Her husband is waiting outside; he will come in if you ask. She was quite tearful at reception.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Thank you, Sister. Come in, have a seat. I am Dr Pillay. What has been worrying you?
[SEG0003] person_3 (PATIENT): Good morning, Doctor. Thank you for seeing me. I believe I am pregnant, and I have had spotting and cramps. I am rather anxious.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): Shame, that is a horrible worry. Tell me about the spotting. When did it begin?
[SEG0005] person_3 (PATIENT): Three days ago. It was light and brownish, and yesterday there was a little red blood, not a great deal.
[SEG0006] person_2 (DOCTOR): And the cramps?
[SEG0007] person_3 (PATIENT): A dull ache, low in the tummy, over the same three days. They come and go. Not terrible, though they kept me awake a little last night. Lying down eases it somewhat.
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): How far along might you be? When was the last period?
[SEG0009] person_3 (PATIENT): I cannot pin it down. The last period was around Diwali, or after. Perhaps eight weeks, perhaps ten. I did not record the date.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): We will not force a date. Was there a positive home test?
[SEG0011] person_3 (PATIENT): Yes. Two home tests, both positive, about a fortnight ago. This is my first pregnancy.
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any heavy bleeding, clots, or soaking a pad?
[SEG0013] person_3 (PATIENT): No. I have not soaked a pad, and there have been no clots.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): Nauseous in the mornings?
[SEG0015] person_3 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose... sometimes, not really. It is difficult to say.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): Pain or burning when you pass urine, or—
[SEG0017] person_3 (PATIENT): No, the urine is normal. The spotting is a little more when I—
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): After you have been walking?
[SEG0019] person_3 (PATIENT): Yes, after the walk from the taxi rank. I am a bookkeeper and I sit most of the day, but that walk stirs it up.
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any dizziness, or feeling faint?
[SEG0021] person_3 (PATIENT): No, I have not felt faint, and I am not dizzy. Worried, yes, but not faint.
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): Which medicines are you on?
[SEG0023] person_3 (PATIENT): Folic acid, five milligrams, one tablet every morning, which the GP started. And a pregnancy vitamin from Clicks, one a day. Nothing besides those.
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any allergies?
[SEG0025] person_3 (PATIENT): No, Doctor. None that I know of.
[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): Operations, or any ongoing illness?
[SEG0027] person_3 (PATIENT): I have never had surgery. I do get migraines from time to time. That is all.
[SEG0028] person_2 (DOCTOR): Sister, please call her husband in. What observations did you get just now?
[SEG0029] person_1 (NURSE): Pressure was one eighteen over seventy-two, pulse eighty-eight, temperature thirty-six point six. I will bring him.
[SEG0030] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Sorry, Doc. Priya, you alright? She hardly slept, and she would not eat breakfast.
[SEG0031] person_2 (DOCTOR): Glad you are here. Has she had any shoulder pain, or pain under the ribs?
[SEG0032] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Nothing like that, no. She just keeps checking the—
[SEG0033] person_3 (PATIENT): The pad, every hour. I am sorry. There is no shoulder pain.
[SEG0034] person_2 (DOCTOR): Please don't apologise. Any miscarriages or clotting problems in the family?
[SEG0035] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Her mom is fine, she— sorry, you go on, Priya.
[SEG0036] person_3 (PATIENT): No, Doctor. No clotting problems and no miscarriages in the family. My mother had two normal pregnancies.
[SEG0037] person_2 (DOCTOR): May I examine your abdomen?
[SEG0038] person_3 (PATIENT): Yes, of course.
[SEG0039] person_2 (DOCTOR): It is soft, with mild tenderness low in the midline. No guarding, and no mass. I will skip an internal examination. I want a scan and blood tests done here this morning.
[SEG0040] person_3 (PATIENT): Certainly. May I ask what the blood tests are?

[SEG0041] person_2 (DOCTOR): A pregnancy hormone level, your blood group, and a full blood count. The scan looks for the site of the pregnancy and a heartbeat. My working impression is a threatened miscarriage, though it may simply be normal early spotting. The tests will decide.
[SEG0042] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Should she still take the folic acid? She missed the vitamin yesterday, she was in a state.

[SEG0043] person_2 (DOCTOR): Yes, continue the folic acid five milligrams every morning, and the vitamin daily. One missed day will not harm. Rest, no heavy lifting, and no intercourse until the scan is back.
[SEG0044] person_3 (PATIENT): I understand. If the bleeding becomes heavier, what should I do?

[SEG0045] person_2 (DOCTOR): If the bleeding soaks a pad within an hour, or the pain is severe, or you feel faint, come straight to casualty and do not wait. Otherwise I will see you here this afternoon with the results.
[SEG0046] person_3 (PATIENT): Thank you, Doctor. We will wait for the scan, and return this afternoon.
